name: How do you keep a custom spa private in a dense neighborhood?

mainEntity.name: How do you keep a custom spa private in a dense neighborhood?
mainEntity.text: How do you keep a custom spa private in a dense neighborhood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Privacy is often one of the biggest design concerns in dense Los Angeles neighborhoods. The most effective approach is to build privacy into the spa layout from the beginning rather than trying to fix it later with random screens. Good options include positioning the spa away from direct second-story views, using perimeter walls or fencing, adding layered landscaping, and orienting seating so users are not exposed to neighboring windows. Raised spa walls, sunken placements, and low-glare lighting can also help create a more secluded feel. In some cases, the surrounding patio, pergola, or cabana can do as much for privacy as the spa itself. Homeowners should think about daytime and nighttime visibility separately because a space that feels private at noon may be exposed after dark. A strong design makes the spa feel like a retreat without blocking airflow or making maintenance difficult.
acceptedAnswer.description: Privacy can be improved with walls, layered planting, raised spa placement, seat orientation, and lighting design that reduces visibility from neighboring homes. The best solution combines screening with a layout that avoids direct sightlines.
